_comment: THE PLAN STAGE LADDER — the single source for what a plan entry's `stage:`
may say, in priority order, for every plan that is NOT the website's.
WHY IT EXISTS. Two vocabularies had grown up side by side and neither was
written down anywhere: `investigate` / `on-hold` / `planned` in the app
entries, and `next` / `planned` / `wip` in Personal Apps' app-list. Nothing
validated either, and — worse — plan-order.js can only parse a VERSION
token (p0.4, v1.0, 1.+), so every one of those words fell through to null
and sorted last. The app plans had priority labels that carried no
priority. This file is the ladder they now answer to.
THE WEBSITE IS NOT GOVERNED BY THIS. site / lifespan-atlas /
chromatic-camelot tag entries with roadmap version tokens, which sort by
number and need no table — see parseVersion in plan-order.js. Their legend
comes from plans/plan-versions.json, build-emitted from site-roadmap.yaml.
This file is the same idea for everything else, and the console builds
serialise it to the same filename so the SAME renderer draws both legends.
THE SHAPE IS plan-versions.json's, deliberately: [{token, title}].
page-widgets/plan-renderer.js already fetches that file and builds a legend
from it — 'a page without it (e.g. a console plan) simply has no legend'.
Matching the shape is what makes the legend appear with no renderer change.
WHY THREE. The only question a plan entry answers is WHEN, and three words
cover it with nothing to look up (user decision 2026-08-24, after `wip` and
`on-hold` were judged jargon). `investigate` was dropped as a stage
because it is a KIND OF WORK, not a time — the task text already says so.
A fourth, `paused` (started then parked, as against never started), was
weighed and left out; adding it is one entry here and nothing else.
JSON, not YAML, because it has readers in TWO languages: plan-order.js and
cli.js on the Node side, the console builds and 日程 Agenda's [p] Planner
on the Python side. JSON is the only format both parse with no dependency,
which is what makes this one file rather than two copies.
_unset_comment: `unset` IS NOT A RUNG OF THE LADDER ABOVE, and that is why it sits in its
own key. The three stages are DECISIONS about when; this is the absence of
one — an entry nobody has placed yet. It therefore applies to the website's
version axis too, which the ladder explicitly does not (see THE WEBSITE IS
NOT GOVERNED BY THIS): 'no stage chosen' is a state of the ENTRY, not a
property of whichever vocabulary that plan tags in. Both legend emitters
append it, so every plan page ends its legend with the same row.
AUTHORED AS ABSENCE. You do not write `stage: unset` in a YAML — you leave
`stage:` off. The token is the RENDERER's name for that hole
(plan-renderer.js has carried it since the filter bar existed: the neutral
tag chrome, the 'unset' filter button, the first step of the click-cycle).
What was missing was only a NAME for it, so a stage-less entry rendered as
an untagged line and the filter button matched nothing. `stage: unset`
written out by hand is still accepted on read — plan_data_check does not
call it off-ladder — because the browser's Save path emits what the cycle
produced.
WHY 'No stage' (user decision 2026-08-25). The alternatives all said more
than they knew: 'Unassigned' leans on a person, 'Undecided' claims you
weighed it, 'Unsorted' claims an order. This one names the empty field and
stops, which is the whole of what is true about such an entry.
